subject: Unexpected differences between plyr and dplyr

messages.author: 438570ef779c59f7
messages.subject: Unexpected differences between plyr and dplyr
parts:
Hi, 

As I started exploring dplyr, I found some unexpected differences between plyr and dplyr that I would like to clarify and understand whether this is intentional or not, and whether there are alternative solutions

Thanks


Two things : 

1. mutate can't handle multiple outputs

# generate a set of observations : 100 obs per category
nobs <- 100
ncat <- 5
cat  <- letters[1:ncat]
data <-  data.frame (cat= rep(cat, each=nobs), val=round(rnorm(nobs*ncat, mean=100,sd=20 ), 0))

# ddply & sumarize works fine
require(plyr)
ddply(data, .(cat), summarise, m= mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))
plyr::summarize(data, m = mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))

# ddply & transform work fine
require(plyr)
ddply(data, .(cat),transform, m= mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))
transform(data, m = mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))

# but neither plyr::mutate nor dplyr::mutate do 

require(plyr)
ddply(data, .(cat), mutate, m= mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))
> Error : wrong result size (11), expected 100 or 1

plyr::mutate(data, m = mean(val), Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))
> Error in `[[<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, col, value = c(36, 75, 81, 88, 93,  : 
  replacement has 1 row, data has 500

require(dplyr)
group_by(data, cat) %.% mutate(m=mean(val))
> OK
group_by(data, cat) %.% mutate(Q=matrix(quantile(val, probs=seq(0,1,0.1)), ncol=11))
> Error : incompatible size (11), expecting 100 (the group size) or 1


# 2. dplyr::mutate can't handle reference to external tables 

# 2. dplyr::mutate can't handle reference to external tables ?

nobs <- 100
ncat <- 5
cat  <- letters[1:ncat]
CAT <-  data.frame(catname=cat, catval = c(10,20,30,40, 50))
data <-  data.frame (num= 1:500, cat= rep(cat, each=nobs),  val=round(rnorm(nobs*ncat, mean=100,sd=20 ), 0))

# this works fine :
data2  <- ddply(data,.(num), mutate, valcat= CAT$catval[CAT$catname==cat]) 
#
# but this does not :
require(dplyr)
mutate (data, valcat= CAT$catval[CAT$catname==cat])
> Error: wrong result size (100), expected 500 or 1
data2 <- data%.% group_by(num) %.% mutate (valcat= CAT$catval[CAT$catname==cat])
> Error: incompatible size (5), expecting 1 (the group size) or 1

# However, the following does work ! 
fc <-  function(c) CAT$catval[CAT$catname==c]
data2 <- data%.% group_by(num) %.% mutate (valcat= fc(cat))

Thanks

Alain

messages.subject: Re: Unexpected differences between plyr and dplyr
parts:
On Sat, Apr 12, 2014 at 12:14 PM, alain content <alain....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> As I started exploring dplyr, I found some unexpected differences between
> plyr and dplyr that I would like to clarify and understand whether this is
> intentional or not, and whether there are alternative solutions
>
> Thanks
>
>
> Two things :
>
> 1. mutate can't handle multiple outputs

It's not multiple outputs that are the problem, its columns that are
matrices. This is something we will eventually support, but we want
to make sure it's well tested.

> # 2. dplyr::mutate can't handle reference to external tables ?
>
> nobs <- 100
> ncat <- 5
> cat <- letters[1:ncat]
> CAT <- data.frame(catname=cat, catval = c(10,20,30,40, 50))
> data <- data.frame (num= 1:500, cat= rep(cat, each=nobs),
> val=round(rnorm(nobs*ncat, mean=100,sd=20 ), 0))
>
> # this works fine :
> data2 <- ddply(data,.(num), mutate, valcat= CAT$catval[CAT$catname==cat])
> #
> # but this does not :
> require(dplyr)
> mutate (data, valcat= CAT$catval[CAT$catname==cat])
>> Error: wrong result size (100), expected 500 or 1
> data2 <- data%.% group_by(num) %.% mutate (valcat=
> CAT$catval[CAT$catname==cat])
>> Error: incompatible size (5), expecting 1 (the group size) or 1

What exactly do you expect this to do? The operation outside of
mutate doesn't make much sense to me:

CAT$catval[CAT$catname == data$cat]

Maybe you mean

CAT$catval[match(data$cat, CAT$catname)] ?

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Unexpected differences between plyr and dplyr
parts:
Hi Hadley, 

Regarding #2, you are absolutely right that using match() does the job perfectly. 

However, I still don't understand two things :

- why the logic that worked with plyr::mutate does not work with dplyr::mutate ? 
I'll try to explain some more  
ie (I reproduce the full context of the example)

nobs <- 100
ncat <- 5
cat  <- letters[1:ncat]
CAT <-  data.frame(catname=cat, catval = c(10,20,30,40, 50))
data <-  data.frame (num= 1:500, cat= rep(cat, each=nobs),  
     val=round(rnorm(nobs*ncat, mean=100,sd=20 ), 0))

The following code works fine : I assume it works because it splits data into one row elements, so the filter on CAT selects a single value

require(plyr)
data2  <- ddply(data,.(num), mutate, valcat= CAT$catval[CAT$catname==cat])

# 

However  what I thought would be the equivalent logic in dplyr does not work, 
(and please note that the error msg is kind of paradoxical !)

require(dplyr)

data2 <- data%.% group_by(num) %.% mutate (valcat= CAT$catval[CAT$catname==cat])

> Error: incompatible size (5), expecting 1 (the group size) or 1

#

- Second, using what (at least to me) seems the same logic but through a function call,  does work !

data2 <- data%.% group_by(num) %.% mutate (valcat= fc(cat))

Thanks again for taking the time to clarify, 
Alain
